intent: Allow verifying a delivery before it is deployed, to record a dry run.

edit.summary:
I added a dry-run verification to `delivery/delivery.domain.yaml`. I didn't run any validation or scenarios.

- **New action `verify_dry_run`:** An approver, who must be a person, can run it on a built delivery before it is deployed. It sets a new optional field, `dry_run_verified`, on DeliveryRequest. It is denied if the request is already deployed or if its harness didn't pass.
- **State matrix:** The action is allowed only in the `built` stage, where it leaves the stage as `built`. It is `n/a` in every other stage. I marked this cell and the action `proposed` rather than `confirmed`, because I couldn't cite an interview line for them. The `source` I gave the action is a placeholder borrowed from an existing line.
- **Unchanged:** A dry run does not set `verified` or move the request to the `verified` stage. The real `verify` action and its invariants are untouched, so a delivery still can't reach `verified` without being deployed and passing its probes.
- **Version:** I bumped the file version from 6 to 7.

I didn't touch the authoring file or the composition file.

findings.problem: dry_run_verified is never cleared. A re-preview (built -> previewing -> built, or from done) produces a new build, and record_build does not reset the flag. The flag also survives a rebuild whose harness fails, and a new deploy. It can therefore claim a dry run on a build that was never rehearsed, or one that has since failed its harness. record_deployment already clears probes_passed for the same reason, and the new flag has no equivalent.
findings.where: delivery.domain.yaml: actions.record_build and actions.record_deployment effects, property dry_run_verified

findings.problem: The new action and its matrix cell cite interview L5 with the quote '전부 다 추천한 거 동의.' ('I agree with all the recommendations'). That line was recorded before this change request and cannot be a person's approval of a dry-run verification. The citation implies owner backing that does not exist. The built/verify_dry_run cell also has no source at all, unlike the neighbouring cells.

No scenario covers verify_dry_run: neither the allowed case on a built request with a passing harness, nor the denials by not-deployed or harness-passed, nor the 'does not verify' guarantee. R2 (built, harness failed) and R4 (done, deployed) are fixtures that would suit this. The new action's behaviour, and the claim that it leaves stage and verified untouched, is therefore never checked.

The glossary defines 'verified' only as a deployed-and-probed state and does not mention a dry run. It also still says that nothing unverified reaches the environment. Nothing explains that dry_run_verified is a separate rehearsal flag that does not satisfy verification or gate deploy. The glossary is stale against the new concept, and readers may take the flag as a deploy gate.

dry_run_verified is set by verify_dry_run but nothing ever clears it. A later preview and record_build produce a new build, or record_deployment runs, and the flag still says the rehearsal passed. That is a stale claim about a build that was never rehearsed. record_deployment clears probes_passed for the same reason, but nothing does the same for the dry run. The flag also gates nothing, because deploy does not read it.

verify_dry_run cites interview line L5, the blanket 'agree to all recommendations' quote. That line was recorded before this change and says nothing about a dry-run verification. The citation does not support the new action, and its matrix cell for built has no source at all.

No scenario exercises verify_dry_run. Neither the allowed case on a built request with a passing harness nor the denials (not-deployed, harness-passed on R2) are covered, and nothing shows that a dry run leaves stage and verified unchanged. The new preconditions reuse ids already used by other actions (not-deployed, harness-passed), so the existing scenarios' denied_by checks do not cover them.

The glossary and the verify and verified descriptions still describe verification only as a post-deploy, probes-passed act. The new dry-run concept, 'verified' versus 'dry-run verified', is not documented. The rule 'only-a-person-deliveryrequest-verified' covers only the verified outcome, and there is no matching rule for dry_run_verified. That permission is carried only by the action's own requires: human.

dry_run_verified is never cleared when the commit is rebuilt. record_build leaves it untouched, so a dry run recorded on one build still reads true after a new preview produces a different build or a failed harness. record_deployment clears probes_passed on a new deploy, but nothing resets the dry-run flag. Nothing reads dry_run_verified either, so it gives no guarantee before deploy.

The new action's provenance does not support it. It cites interview line L5 with the generic quote '전부 다 추천한 거 동의' (agreed to all the recommendations), which predates this request and says nothing about dry runs or the added harness-passed and not-deployed preconditions. The preconditions and the matrix cell carry no source of their own, so the rehearsal rule looks confirmed by an interview that never discussed it.
findings.where: delivery.domain.yaml: actions.verify_dry_run source and preconditions; transitions built.verify_dry_run

findings.problem: dry_run_verified is never cleared. record_build overwrites harness_ok when a commit is re-previewed, and record_deployment clears probes_passed on a new deploy. Neither resets dry_run_verified. A request whose rebuild failed its harness, or that has since been deployed, still shows a dry run as done. This is inconsistent with how probes_passed is handled, and the flag now describes a build that no longer exists.
findings.where: delivery.domain.yaml: actions record_build / record_deployment, property dry_run_verified

findings.problem: The new action has no scenario. Neither the allowed case (built with a passing harness leaves the stage at built and sets dry_run_verified) nor the two denials (not-deployed, harness-passed on R2) is exercised. The stage cells that are n/a for it are not exercised either.

The action's source cites interview line L5, 'agree to all the recommendations', which was recorded before this change request. That line cannot be the owner's agreement to a dry-run verification feature, so the provenance is misleading. The new transition cell also has no source.

The glossary and the 'verified' definition were not updated to say what a dry run is or that it is not verification. The new flag dry_run_verified has a name very close to verified. The purpose and rules still say only verify makes a verified deployment, and nothing states that dry_run_verified must not satisfy or replace the probes-passed requirement for real verification.

dry_run_verified is set to true and never cleared. record_build, preview and record_deployment do not reset it. If a built commit is dry-run verified and then rebuilt (built -> preview -> previewing -> built) and the new harness fails, or the request is redeployed, the flag still says the dry run happened. findings.problem: No scenario covers verify_dry_run. Nothing checks that it is allowed from built with a passing harness, denied by harness-passed or not-deployed, or that it leaves the stage at built and leaves verified false. Nothing checks that verify still needs a deployment and passed probes.

The glossary defines 'verified' and 'preview' but not a dry run. The 'verified' entry reads as the only kind of verification, while the new action adds a second, weaker one that does not mean verified. The new action's description relies on that distinction.
